securityFixWave.trigger: Cold security review returned 1 CRITICAL, 2 MEDIUM, 2 LOW after the first verify pass. All five closed in a bounded fix wave; this verify.json reflects the post-fix tree.

findings.issue: toSingleLine escaped C0+DEL but never < or >, so an attacker-authored envelope could emit a literal close tag, terminate the containment block early, and append forged out-of-band text into agent context at turn zero. ~630 attacker-chosen characters per entry across 5 entries. The attacker also controlled placement: createdAt is an unconstrained z.string().min(1) and list() sorts ascending on it, so a far-future value put the malicious entry last, making the forged block the final thing in context.
findings.fix: (a) < (0x3C) and > (0x3E) added to CONTROL_CHAR_RE, rendered as \x3c / \x3e. (b) Per-invocation crypto.randomUUID() nonce on both tags, sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9-] so a nonce cannot itself carry a delimiter. Both halves shipped - (a) is the primary control, (b) is defense in depth for any future unescaped field.
findings.evidence: ORCHESTRATOR-EXECUTED exploit probe on the post-fix tree: an envelope carrying a literal close tag in intent AND origin.repoName AND origin.repoPath, with createdAt 2099 to force last position, yields close-tag occurrences = 1 (expect 1) and no raw < or > in the attacker-controlled entry line. VERDICT: FORGERY BLOCKED. Executor's independent probe agrees, and additionally confirms the notice ends with the real nonce'd close and that the injected 'system-reminder' text remains VISIBLE but escaped rather than silently dropped.

findings.issue: resolveMailboxDir guarded emptiness but not absoluteness. mailboxDirFor is a bare join(homedir, '.luca/handoff'), so HOME='.' yielded a relative path resolved against cwd - the hook would read the CURRENT REPO's .luca/handoff/ as the machine-global mailbox. That directory, unlike ~/.luca/handoff (0700, home-denied), is repo-local and writable by the agent's own Write tool, making a checked-in .luca/handoff/*.json a prompt-injection delivery vector requiring no mailbox access.
findings.evidence: resolveMailboxDir('.'), ('tmp'), ('./sub'), ('../up'), ('') all return null; fail-closed arm asserts an absolute home still resolves; e2e spawn with HOME='.' against a planted repo-local decoy stays silent.

findings.issue: Escape class covered U+0000-U+001F and U+007F only. U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR, U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR and U+0085 NEL are line terminators, so the 'exactly one line' invariant did not hold. Bidi overrides and zero-width characters could also visually reorder or hide text in the human-facing luca handoff list view that shares this escaper.
findings.fix: Class extended (all via String.fromCharCode/range, never a literal class) to C1 0x80-0x9F, 0x200B-0x200F, 0x2028-0x202E, 0x2066-0x2069, 0xFEFF. Emitter widened to \uNNNN above 0xFF so nothing is dropped.
findings.evidence: Tests assert no LS/PS/NEL/RLO/ZWSP/BOM code point survives, escapes are present, and a clean path passes through unchanged.

findings.issue: main().then(ok, exit0) did not cover a throw during MODULE EVALUATION - the top-level static imports. A bad bundle or version skew would print an uncaught stack trace at every session start in every repo, which is this feature's worst possible regression.
findings.fix: Both paths into luca-core are now await import(...) inside main - the transport AND ./resolve-mailbox-dir.ts, which statically imported mailboxDirFor. Deferring only the transport would have been a no-op. render-inbox-notice.ts stays static (type-only import, erased at build).
findings.evidence: Test asserts both dynamic forms are present and that no static import line mentions luca-core or resolve-mailbox-dir. Also defers cost past both existsSync fast-exits, tightening the perf budget.

findings.issue: Both cappers sliced on code-unit indices, so a boundary inside a surrogate pair emitted a lone surrogate that JSON.stringify + stdout.write cannot encode as valid UTF-8 - malformed output on the exact channel the harness parses. Attacker-triggerable by padding intent with astral-plane characters.
findings.fix: New exported capCodePoints() truncates on code points; used by toSingleLine (256) and preview (120).
findings.evidence: Tests sweep pad lengths 115-125 with astral padding: no lone surrogate, JSON to UTF-8 round-trip identity.

THREE EXECUTOR DEVIATIONS DURING EXECUTION WERE ALL TRUE VACUITY CATCHES: (1) ac-25 - HOME='' cannot make a process observe an empty homedir because POSIX os.homedir() falls back to the passwd DB, so the planned probe was green either way; the replacement is STRICTLY STRONGER, proving the planted decoy is reachable at join(repo, mailboxDirFor({homedir:''})); (2) the escaper was rebuilt via String.fromCharCode rather than moved verbatim because writing the literal class put RAW CONTROL CHARACTERS on disk - cntrl grep over the four sources now returns no matches and parity with the phase-2 original is structurally identical; (3) ac-09 - OPEN_TAG contains an 'x', so the planned /x+/ first-match returned length 1 and passed against an uncapped renderer; replaced with a longest-run assertion. THREE RESIDUAL VACUITY FINDINGS, ALL NON-BLOCKING, CARRIED TO PHASE 4: (a) ac-26 cannot distinguish degradation path 6 from path 7 - deleting the !listed.ok guard makes renderInboxNotice(undefined) throw into the catch-all, which still exits 0 silently; the discriminated union is the compensating control. (b) ac-25 pins the pure guard and the mechanism but not the CALL SITE at handler.ts:105 - deleting the null-check alone leaves every case green, with typecheck as the compensating control. (c) ac-09 asserts against the module's own MAX_INTENT_PREVIEW, so raising the constant keeps both the registered check and the unit test green. LIVE-SESSION OBSERVATION - GENUINE BUT NARROWER THAN THE PHRASE IMPLIES: it is a direct invocation of the BUNDLED dist handler with real stdin, NOT Claude Code firing SessionStart. Every reported fact is independently corroborated (the bundle exists and contains the renderer and guard; the block matches render-inbox-notice.ts line-for-line; the absent ellipsis is consistent with a sub-120-char intent), so it was not fabricated - but the matcher-spelling risk it was meant to close is actually closed by ac-04/ac-05/ac-06, not by this observation. The orchestrator's earlier characterization of it as proving the payoff 'works end to end' overstated it.
